11645298.description: Part of a large traffic queue in Staplers Road, Staplers , Newport , Isle of Wight . Being the summer holidays, lots of tourists were holidaying on the island. Whenever the weather is a bit nasty, everyone decides to go to Newport for the day, which results in the whole place becoming extremely congested, sometimes nearly gridlocked. This day was one such occasion (it poured down soon afterwards). On this occasion, traffic had queued back past the last houses on Staplers Road. When I hit the congestion, the end of the queue was about half way between the junctions with Mews Lane and Blacklands Road. I had been on the number 9 bus (as seen in File:Southern Vectis 194 HW52 EPP and Newport Staplers Road traffic queue.JPG ), but from past experience decided to get off and walk, as did the two people walking down the pavement in the photo, and walk the rest of the mile and a quarter journey into Newport. I walked past the traffic queue and easily beat the bus.

127447713.description: Notebook belonging to Georg Bredig (1868-1944). Contents have notes from lectures by Herman Francis Mark (1895-1992). Mark was an Austrian chemist known for his contributions to polymer science, X-ray diffraction, and his work at IG Farben. In 1938 Mark began preparing to leave Austria but Hitler invaded Austria before he could leave the country. Mark was sent to a Gestapo prison. After his release, he was able to immigrate to America by first entering Canada. He continued his research in polymers in Brooklyn, New York.

153580501.description: Deccafax Viewdata Terminal Model VP1, manufactured by Decca Radio and Television, London, England, 1979-1994. Editing Keyboard Type UB80-0023, by Cherry GmbH, possibly Germany, 1979-1994. Serial No 4486. Prestel was the brand name for the Post Office's Viewdata system. Viewdata enabled subscribers to access information from a remote database. Users typed text commands to navigate through pages of information and communicated using'Prestel Mailbox'. Viewdata was developed by Samuel Fedida, an engineer in the Post Office Research Department. Prestel itself was commercially launched in 1979, and achieved a maximum of 90,000 subscribers before it was eventually sold in 1994. This Prestel unit was used by the House Of Commons until 1994.

157884599.api_title: File:Blank Notebook Given to Charles Lindbergh by Estelle Carpenter - DPLA - 445cdea0eb7306d3abdaa5dcae36ce0f (page 1).jpg
157884599.credit: This file was contributed to Wikimedia Commons by Missouri Historical Society as part of a cooperation project. The donation was facilitated by the Digital Public Library of America , via its partner Heartland Hub . Record in source catalog DPLA identifier: 445cdea0eb7306d3abdaa5dcae36ce0f Missouri Historical Society identifier: 1927-053-0545
157884599.description: This small notebook was made in Czechoslovakia around the mid 1920s and was sold by the Hampshire Book Shop of Northampton, Massachusetts. The book was given to Charles A. Lindbergh in 1927 by Estelle Carpenter, the director of music for the San Francisco public schools, on behalf of herself and the students of the San Francisco schools. Her business card and a handwritten note appear near the back of the blank book: "Miss Estelle Carpenter / Director of Music, of / San Francisco / Public School. / and all Pupils / of San Francisco / Cal." Lindbergh loaned the book to the Missouri Historical Society in 1927, and he gave it to the Society in 1933.

157938617.api_title: File:Chinese Rosewood and Inlay Desk Chair Displayed at the 1904 World's Fair - DPLA - 713985f10aa9df1993795ebe86e7cba9 (page 1).jpg
157938617.credit: This file was contributed to Wikimedia Commons by Missouri Historical Society as part of a cooperation project. The donation was facilitated by the Digital Public Library of America , via its partner Heartland Hub . Record in source catalog DPLA identifier: 713985f10aa9df1993795ebe86e7cba9 Missouri Historical Society identifier: 1977-114-0001
157938617.description: This Chinese Rosewood swivel desk chair with bone or ivory inlay designs was exhibited at the Chinese Exhibit in the Palace of Manufacturers at the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition. The chair was made in Ningbo, China sometime in the few years before the fair. It is in the Shanghai style of Chinese furniture, a style that combined traditional Chinese materials and decoration with Western styling primarily for sale to Western audiences. It features carved openwork and ornate inlay displaying Chinese plants, animals, architecture, and symbolism. The chair was purchased along with a desk from the exhibit after the fair and shipped to San Francisco, California. The chair and the desk were purchased from an antiques dealer in 1937 by Frank C. Dougherty, and they were donated to the Missouri Historical Society by his son Howard William Dougherty in 1977.

157959925.description: This oak desk chair was used by Paul J. Morrin, former president of the AFL International Association of Bridge, Structural & Ornamental Iron Workers from 1918-1948. The chair was manufactured by Conrades Manufacturing Company in Saint Louis, Missouri. It is a swivel chair that also leans back, and it has a saddle seat, arms, and banister back. The chair was given to Nicholas and Dorothy Esser by Josephine Morrin, Paul Morrin's widow, sometime between 1951-1970. Dorothy Esser donated it to the Missouri Historical Society in 1993.

15954756.description: This mugs is covered in stars, until you fill it with a hot beverage. As soon as you pour in a hot coffee the mug’s appearance quickly changes. Within a minute, most of the stars will give way to the stripes…and you are left with a patriotic mug!

15955545.description: A Thermochromic mug. The cold mug displays the sleeping face white on black. When you pour in the hot coffee, the mug’s appearance quickly changes. Within a minute, the black mug has become completely white and the face will have awoken to greet you. What a way to start the day!

15955686.description: A Thermochromic mug. The cold mug displays the ‘COLD’ message white on blue. Pour in the hot coffee and the mug’s appearance quickly changes. Within a minute, the blue mug will become completely white and the message will magically transform to…‘HOT’ red on white!

15955760.description: A Thermochromic mug. The cold mug displays the ‘OFF’ message white on black. When you pour in the hot coffee, the mug’s appearance quickly changes. Within a minute, the black mug has become completely white and the message has magically transformed to…‘ON’ black on white!

163764849.description: A stapler is not just a stapler. When I was a kid I had this little Swingline stapler, red and just the right size for a little kid's hand. I loved to be able to staple my school assignments with multiple pages together before turning them in. I was really into school supplies. Mechanical pencils. Cartridge pens. Nifty folders. As a teacher I've been using staplers for years. The Swingline staplers supplied by schools jam all the time. They're hard to reload and it never seems like the right staples are stocked in the supply room. I'm a frustrated and demanding office supply consumer. I have a half dozen staplers in my room at any given time, and I'm lucky to have one that actually works. This past week and made another raid on the supply room and found this old Acco 40. I took it back to my room. I had report cards to staple, for pity sake, and there was no time to be beta-testing staples, but what was I do do? This looked like a classic, sturdy, the parts moved far more smoothly than any Swingline I've had. It worked smoothly, reliably. I didn't pinch myself reloading it and it DIDN'T JAM. I've seen them around for years, but I don't believe I've ever had one. I'm not sure you can get them new any more. I just hope I can get the right staples for it. I've got to hide it from the kids, though, or they'll break it. I'm gonna leave out some Swinglines that are already broken to lure them away from the Acco. Stacked macro with Zerene Stacker.

17679765.description: AMX Mouse (Type 2) inside. The AMX Mouse (Type 2) is almost identical to the Acorn Archimedes Mouse and unlike the Type 1 AMX Mouse, I have seen it in an advertisement for the AMX Mouse for the Electron. It is a 3 button mouse, which connects to the user port. The serial no. is 130137. The insides of the mouse showing the ball, the horizontal and vertical rollers atached to the perforated wheels, the sprung roller which maintains pressure on the ball, the 2 sets of sensors on the larger circuit board which detect the movement of the perforated wheels and the termination of the mouse cable.

17702700.credit: Chris's Acorns: Acorn A500 mouse Direct
17702700.description: Acorn A500 mouse (top).This mouse is from the Acorn A500 , the Archimedes prototype. It connects to the A500 keboard via a 9pin D plug. Although it is a 3 button mouse it is very different from other Acorn mice. It is made by Penny and Giles and is reportedly similar to the mice used on some defence contracts.

17702702.credit: Chris's Acorns: Acorn A500 mouse Direct
17702702.description: Acorn A500 Mouse (bottom).This mouse is from the Acorn A500 , the Archimedes prototype. It connects to the A500 keboard via a 9pin D plug. Although it is a 3 button mouse it is very different from other Acorn mice. It is made by Penny and Giles and is reportedly similar to the mice used on some defence contracts.

17702973.credit: Chris's Acorns: Acorn Archimedes Mouse (Type 1) Direct
17702973.description: Acorn Archimedes Mouse (Type 1) (insides).The Acorn Archimedes Mouse (Type 1) was supplied with the original Archemedes range (A300, A400 and A400/1). It is a 3 button mouse, which all Acorn computers used, and plugged into the top right hand side of the keyboard. The Acorn part number is 176,003. Note this mouse is almost identical to the AMX Mouse (Type 2). The pictures show: The insides of the mouse showing the ball, the horizontal and vertical rollers atached to the perforated wheels, the sprung roller which maintains pressure on the ball, the 2 sets of sensors on the larger circuit board which detect the movement of the perforated wheels and the termination of the mouse cable.

17703078.description: Acorn Mouse (Type 2) (bottom).This 3 button mouse replaced the Archimedes Mouse (Type 1) and was shipped with the A5000, and maybe with the A3000, so I have called it the Acorn Mouse (Type 2), The mouse is made by Logitech and is a model M-PF7. The Acorn part number is 183,180. The pictures show: The bottom of the mouse showing the Logitech label, the Acorn serial number (25-ALB12-1014659 - ALB12 is the product code for an A5000), the mouse ball with a removable collar which enables you to clean it and the 4 circular plastic pads which the mouse slides on.

17703089.description: Acorn Mouse (Type 3) with top removed.This 3 button mouse replaced the Acorn Mouse Mk2 and was shipped with the A30x0 & A4000, and maybe with the A5000, so I have called it the Acorn Mouse (Type 3), The mouse is made by Logitech and is a model M-PG15. The Acorn part number is 0914,000. The pictures show: The mouse with the top cover removed showing the 3 switches which detect the button clicks at the top, the ball, rollers and sensors in the middle and the mouse cable termination on the right.

17703093.description: Acorn Mouse (Type 4) (bottom).This 3 button mouse replaced the Acorn Mouse Mk3 and was shipped with the Risc PC, so I have called it the Acorn Mouse (Type 4), The mouse is made by Logitech and is a model M-P30. The Acorn part number is 0914,002. The pictures show: The bottom of the mouse showing the Acorn serial number (72-ACB25-1015512 - ACB25 is the product code for a Risc PC 600), the mouse ball with a removable collar which enables you to clean it, the Logitech label and the 4 circular plastic pads which the mouse slides on. This mouse came with my original Risc PC 600 which I bought in 1994.

184983466.credit: Own work designed with Sketchup and rendered with V-Ray
184983466.description: A headset computer is a wearable personal computer that places a transparent near-eye OLED display in the user’s field of view, with adjustable brightness and transparency. The display module includes forward-facing cameras, an illumination light, and a microphone. The visor assembly can rotate upward over the head to move the screen out of view when not in use. The system uses a tethered pocket-PC for processing, battery power, wireless data, and I/O, connected by a USB-C cable routed under the user’s clothing, with audio delivered through a single-ear speaker. A smartphone can function as the primary pointing device by using its camera and flash for surface tracking and by interpreting taps and swipes on the touchscreen as mouse inputs, or could also be used as a trackpad. A future implementation could integrate a dedicated optical navigation sensor into the back of the phone to improve tracking resolution and responsiveness, using the small clearance naturally provided by many phone cases. The setup can be paired with compact portable keyboards that include protective covers with integrated batteries and can also be used with tablets such as iPads. The system would initially function primarily as a conventional personal computer, while augmented reality applications could be developed using the forward-facing cameras and onboard sensors.

36201883.api_title: File:Bottle of medicinal water, France, 1928 Wellcome L0057444.jpg
36201883.description: The bottle of medicinal water on the far left was collected from the hot spring of St Roch at the spa town of Bagnères de Bigorre in south-west France. Hot springs and mineral waters were popular in a number of ancient cultures – including Greek and Roman. Centuries later, a renewed interest in the healing and medicinal properties of these natural waters reached a peak in the Victorian period with hundreds of sites across Europe packed with visitors coming to ‘take the waters’ in the hope of a cure. The handwritten label gives the date, “17 March 1928”, the temperature of the spring, “47ºC” (117ºF), and indicates that it is to be used for the nerves. Once cooled the water was either drunk or applied to the body. St Roch, a pilgrim from Montpellier, France, during the 1300s, was said to cure plague and other infectious diseases. As a saint, he is one of several who was commonly invoked against the plague. 37068850.description: Tea is of course a great British tradition, though the tea plant itself comes from Asia. As can be seen, the vast majority of British people drink tea with milk. Nowadays many people, perhaps most, drink tea from a small bag in a mug such as this for convenience, but it has to be said that the best tea is served in china teacups in saucers poured from a teapot with the tea loose inside. I don't know why. It just does, though that process takes five minutes rather than the one minute in the mug above. Some prefer tea weak whilst others have it so strong a spoon will stand on its end in the cup. Well, not quite...

Text Appearing Before Image: set down. The outlines cover the work that all must do; they do not limit in quantity or method whatmay be done; they should materially increase the time available for the teacher to work out hisown best ideas in history teaching. The Chronological Table, pages 138-140, which may be used in a general review, will be ofassistance in gaining perspective. The blank pages at the back are for notes on outside reading,review topics, etc. Here also may be placed further maps, drawings, etc. These may be madevery successfully by copying the given map with tracing paper, and pasting the tracing paperinto the notebook. The effect is especially good if colored inks are used. These outlines were made for our own school, where they have been satisfactorily triedout. It is gratifying to have arranged the work in consultation with Mr. Walker, and also tohave had the benefit of suggestions from the several colleagues who are teaching English historywith me. 61113875.api_title: File:Physical keyboard layouts comparison ANSI ISO KS ABNT JIS.png
61113875.description: A comparison of common mechanical computer keyboard layouts. Keys that are not present in all of them are highlighted in pink (alphanumeric) and dark-grey (modifier). Keys that are sometimes omitted are shown with dashed outlines. Note that the 104th key in the ABNT layout is located in the numpad section and therefore not shown. These layouts match the “key arrangements” listed in Annex B of the standard ISO/IEC 9995-2 Keyboard layouts for text and office systems — Part 2: Alphanumeric section (as published in January 2026). From left to right, top to bottom: * 101 keyboard, common in North America, Asia, Oceania (ISO key arrangement A) * 101 alternate, common in Asia and Russia (ISO key arrangement L) * 102 keyboard, common in Europe, Latin America (ISO key arrangement E) * 103 keyboard, used in South Korea (ISO key arrangement K) * 104 keyboard, used in Brazil (ISO key arrangement B) * 106 keyboard, used in Japan (ISO key arrangement J)
